info.title: [PREVIEW] Revolut Wallet Loyalty Callbacks
info.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Loyalty endpoints you host and Revolut calls. Implement them to this contract so customers can
enrol in your loyalty program from Revolut Wallet, and so their loyalty cards are applied
automatically when they pay with a Revolut card. Revolut is always the client; you are the
server.

- **Enrol a customer automatically (optional)**: `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` registers the
  customer without any customer interaction, using the details they agreed to share: their
  name, email, and phone number, verified by Revolut's know your customer (KYC) checks, plus
  any partner-configured fields they enter. If the customer must act in a browser (accept
  your terms, provide missing details), return a `403` UI-required code and Revolut falls
  back to the browser flow. If you don't implement auto-enrol, Revolut starts every new
  enrolment with the browser flow.
- **Enrol through the browser flow on your authorisation server**: Revolut reads your
  OpenID Connect discovery document, pushes the authorisation request (`POST /oauth2/par`)
  with `prompt=create`, sends the customer's browser to `GET /oauth2/authorize`, exchanges the
  code at `POST /oauth2/token`, and fetches the membership from `GET /loyalty/profile`.
- **Link a customer's existing account**: when the customer starts "Link existing account" in
  Revolut Wallet, or auto-enrol returns `account_exists`, Revolut runs the same browser flow
  with `prompt=login` and shares no personal data: the customer signs in to you and consents
  to link their membership.
- **Apply a loyalty card to a transaction**: `POST /loyalty/apply`. After a customer enrolled
  in your loyalty program pays with a Revolut card at your business, Revolut asks you to apply
  their loyalty card and report the points earned.

Passes themselves are managed through the companion APIs: the Revolut-hosted
[Wallet Partner API](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/api/revolut-wallet-partner) and the pass endpoints you host in the
[Wallet Partner Callbacks API](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/api/revolut-wallet-callbacks).

**Where the endpoints live.** `POST /loyalty/apply`, `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol`, and
`GET /loyalty/profile` live under the callback base URL you register during onboarding. The
authorisation-server endpoints live under the issuer URL you register, which may include a
path: Revolut reads `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` and calls the endpoint URLs it
lists, so the `/oauth2/*` paths in this reference are illustrative. All `servers` URLs are
examples.

:::info
Start with the [Revolut Wallet guide](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/introduction) and [Get started](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/get-started) to onboard your business.
:::

tags.name: Loyalty enrolment
tags.description:
Enrol customers in your loyalty program from Revolut Wallet, or link a membership they
already have with you: automatic enrolment, the OAuth 2.0 browser flow on your
authorisation server, and the loyalty profile Revolut reads when the flow completes. Both
enrolment and linking record the partner-issued `member_id` and `program_id`, which Revolut
later sends on `POST /loyalty/apply`.

:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

tags.name: Loyalty auto-apply
tags.description:
Auto-apply loyalty cards to Revolut-card transactions. Revolut sends the partner-issued
membership and program identifiers recorded during enrolment or linking, together with the
transaction context you use to match the purchase. Revolut uses the merchant ID and
acquiring institution ID you provide during onboarding to route eligible transactions. The
acquiring institution ID is routing data and is not included in the callback request.

:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

post.summary: Apply a loyalty card to a transaction
post.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Revolut calls this after detecting an eligible Revolut-card transaction by a customer enrolled
in your loyalty program. Locate the active membership using `member_id` and `program_id`, match
the purchase from `transaction_context`, apply the loyalty card, and award the points earned.

**Transaction matching:** `rrn` + `merchant_id` is the primary key; once you have a
candidate, validate `transaction_at` (±24 hours) and require `total.currency` and the decimal
numeric value of `total.amount` to match exactly. The `LoyaltyTransactionContext` schema
documents the authoritative algorithm and collision handling.

If `member_id` and `program_id` do not identify an active membership, return `404` with
`membership_not_found`. If the membership is active but the purchase earns no points under
your program rules, return `200` with `outcome` set to `no_points_earned` and `0` points.

**Idempotency (this operation has side effects on your side):** Revolut sends one
`Idempotency-Key` for each logical apply operation and reuses it for every retry. If the
operation has already completed, return the original successful result without awarding
points again. Reusing the same key with a different request body returns `409`. Do not store
`202`, `429`, or `503` as the final result for a key; Revolut retries them with the same key.

**Status semantics (these drive Revolut's retry behaviour):**
- `200`: loyalty card applied; return the `outcome`, the points earned, and optionally the new balance (`0` points with `no_points_earned` when the purchase earns no points).
- `202`: transaction not ready yet (settlement lag); Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.
- `404`: transaction or active membership definitively not found; Revolut stops retrying.
- `409`: the `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different request body, or the transaction match is ambiguous (`ambiguous_transaction`); Revolut stops retrying.
- `410`: transaction existed but is void (refund/cancellation); Revolut stops.
- `429` / `503`: temporary capacity issue; Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.

:::note
Validate Revolut's credentials (mutual TLS (mTLS), JSON Web Signature (JWS), or OAuth 2.0) and reject any unauthenticated request with `401`.
:::

200.description:
Loyalty card applied. Returns the `outcome`, the points the transaction earned, and,
optionally, the customer's new balance.

points_earned.summary: Points earned, with the new balance

zero_points.summary: Applied, but the purchase earned no points

202.description:
Transaction accepted but not ready yet (settlement lag). Revolut retries,
honouring `Retry-After`.

:::note
Return no body with `202`.
:::

404.description:
The transaction or active loyalty membership is definitively not found. Revolut stops
retrying.

value.message: No transaction found for this rrn and merchant_id.
No active membership found for this member_id and program_id.

410.description: Transaction is void (refund/cancellation). Revolut will stop retrying.

value.message: The transaction is void due to a refund or cancellation.

post.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Revolut calls this when a customer enrols in your loyalty program from Revolut Wallet, to
register them without any customer interaction. The request carries the details the
customer agreed to share: their name, email, and phone number, verified by Revolut's know
your customer (KYC) checks, plus any partner-configured fields they enter. Create the
membership and return its identifiers plus the complete loyalty pass envelope.

This endpoint is optional: tell the Revolut Wallet team during onboarding whether you
implement it. If you don't, Revolut starts every new enrolment with the OAuth 2.0 browser
flow (`POST /oauth2/par` with `prompt=create`).

If the customer must act in a browser (accept your terms, provide missing data), return
`403` with the matching UI-required code below and Revolut falls back to the OAuth 2.0
browser flow. Revolut does not retry the auto-enrol after a `403`.

Revolut does not call this endpoint when the customer starts "Link existing account" in
Revolut Wallet: that flow goes straight to the OAuth 2.0 browser flow with `prompt=login`
and no enrolment claims.

**Never silently link an existing membership:** if the shared data matches an existing
account, return `403` with `account_exists`. Revolut then runs the link flow, where the
customer signs in to you and consents to link their membership. Never create a duplicate
membership.

**Never succeed silently when the customer must accept terms or complete a step:** return
the matching `403` code instead.

**Idempotency (this operation has side effects on your side):** Revolut sends one
`Idempotency-Key` for each logical enrolment and reuses it for every retry. If the
enrolment has already completed, return the original `200` without creating another
membership. Reusing the same key with a different request body returns `409`. Do not
store `429` or `503` as the final result for a key; Revolut retries them with the
same key. Retain completed keys and their responses for at least 7 days.

**Status semantics (these drive Revolut's retry behaviour):**
- `200`: membership created; return the `member_id`, `program_id`, and the complete pass envelope.
- `403`: UI-required (see the codes below); Revolut never retries and falls back to the OAuth 2.0 browser flow. `insufficient_scope` is terminal.
- `400` / `401`: terminal; Revolut stops retrying.
- `409`: the `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different request body; Revolut stops retrying.
- `429` / `503`: temporary capacity issue; Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.

:::note
Validate Revolut's credentials (OAuth 2.0 client credentials, optionally hardened with mutual TLS (mTLS)) and reject any unauthenticated request with `401`.
:::

auto_enrol.summary: Automatic enrolment with the shared enrolment claims

200.description:
Membership created. Return the identifiers of the new membership and the complete
loyalty pass envelope for the customer's Revolut Wallet.

enrolled.summary: Membership created, with the complete pass envelope

403.description:
The customer must complete steps in the browser (UI-required), or the token lacks
the required scope. Revolut never retries a UI-required response; it falls back to
the OAuth 2.0 browser flow with the `prompt` value shown below. `insufficient_scope`
is terminal: fix the credentials during onboarding.

| Code | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `ui_required` | Generic: the customer must complete steps in the browser before enrolment. Revolut starts the browser flow with `prompt=create`. |
| `account_exists` | The shared data matches an existing membership; never create a duplicate. Revolut starts the link flow: `prompt=login` and no enrolment claims. |
| `terms_acceptance_required` | The customer must accept your Terms and Conditions in the browser. Revolut starts the browser flow with `prompt=create`. |
| `additional_data_required` | Enrolment needs data the customer must provide in the browser. Revolut starts the browser flow with `prompt=create`. |
| `insufficient_scope` | Token lacks `loyalty.enrol` (terminal): fix credentials during onboarding. Revolut doesn't start the browser flow. |

value.message: The customer must complete steps in the browser before enrolment.
The shared data matches an existing membership; the customer must sign in and link it in the browser.
The customer must accept the Terms and Conditions in the browser.
Enrolment requires data the customer must provide in the browser.
The token does not have the loyalty.enrol scope.

get.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Your OpenID Connect discovery document (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0). Revolut reads it
from `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`, using the issuer URL you register
during onboarding, to find your Pushed Authorization Request (PAR), authorisation, and
token endpoints and the keys that sign your ID tokens. Revolut then calls the URLs the
document lists. Serve it publicly over HTTPS; it carries no secrets.

Your document can list more values than this reference requires, for example extra grant
types or `prompt` values. Revolut relies on the following:
- PAR is mandatory (`require_pushed_authorization_requests: true`) and PKCE uses `S256`.
- Authorisation responses carry `iss` (RFC 9207), so Revolut can tell your authorisation
  server apart from other partners' servers that share its redirect URI.
- `prompt_values_supported` includes `login` and `create`.
- `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` includes `RS256`, as OpenID Connect Discovery
  requires. `ES256` is also accepted; the algorithm you sign with is agreed when Revolut's
  client is registered during onboarding.
- `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` includes the client-authentication method
  registered for Revolut: `client_secret_post`, `private_key_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, or
  `self_signed_tls_client_auth`. Revolut never uses `client_secret_basic`.
- `grant_types_supported` includes `client_credentials` if you implement
  `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` or accept OAuth 2.0 on `POST /loyalty/apply`.

Keep the previous signing key in your JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) while you rotate keys, so
ID tokens signed with it still verify.

parameters.description: Revolut's correlation ID for this request. You may ignore it; echoing it is optional on authorisation-server endpoints.

metadata.summary: Metadata for an authorisation server that accepts client secret and private key JWT client authentication

post.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

OAuth 2.0 Pushed Authorization Request (PAR) endpoint (RFC 9126): the
`pushed_authorization_request_endpoint` in your discovery document. Revolut's backend calls
it before sending the customer's browser to your authorisation endpoint, so the enrolment
claims travel over a server-to-server channel instead of through the browser. Store the
request and return a single-use `request_uri`.

Revolut pushes one of the following variants:
- **Enrol a new member**: `prompt` is `create` and `enrolment_claims` carries the details
  the customer agreed to share. Revolut sends it after `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` returns
  a UI-required `403` other than `account_exists`, or directly when you don't implement
  auto-enrol.
- **Link an existing account**: `prompt` is `login` and `enrolment_claims` is `{}`, so no
  personal data is shared. Revolut sends it when the customer starts "Link existing
  account" in Revolut Wallet, or after `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` returns
  `account_exists`.

Both variants carry Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE, RFC 7636): store `code_challenge`
with the request and verify the `code_verifier` Revolut sends to your token endpoint.
Both also carry `program_id` when you operate several loyalty programs.

Authenticate Revolut's client credentials (client secret, private key JSON Web Token
(JWT), or mutual TLS (mTLS), as registered during onboarding) and reject any
unauthenticated request with `401` (`invalid_client`). Unless mTLS is the registered
method, Revolut sends a client secret or JWT assertion in the request body; that's why
`security` lists mTLS as optional.

The `request_uri` must expire after `expires_in` seconds (60–90) and be consumable
exactly once at your authorisation endpoint.

parameters.description: Revolut's correlation ID for this request. You may ignore it; echoing it is optional on authorisation-server endpoints.

pushed_request.summary: Enrol a new member: registration screen, enrolment claims shared

pushed_link_request.summary: Link an existing account: forced sign-in, no personal data shared

201.description:
Authorisation request stored. Return the single-use `request_uri` and how long it
stays valid.

400.description:
Malformed or invalid pushed request, for example a missing `code_challenge`. The
body uses the standard OAuth 2.0 error format (RFC 6749, section 5.2, as applied by
RFC 9126).

value.error_description: The request is missing a required parameter or is otherwise malformed.

401.description:
Client authentication failed (`invalid_client`): Revolut's client credentials are
missing, unknown, or invalid for the registered client-authentication method.

get.summary: Authorise the customer in the browser
get.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Your authorisation endpoint: the `authorization_endpoint` in your discovery document. The
customer's browser (a secure system browser, never an embedded web view) opens it with
the `request_uri` Revolut pushed at `POST /oauth2/par`. Look up the stored request, check
that `client_id` matches the client the `request_uri` was issued to (RFC 9126), and route
the customer by the stored `prompt` value. Route only on `prompt`, never on whether
`enrolment_claims` is empty:

- `prompt=login` (link an existing account): route the customer straight to your sign-in
  screen and force re-authentication, ignoring any existing session. After the customer
  signs in, ask for consent to link their loyalty membership. If the customer has no
  account with you, redirect back with `error=access_denied`.
- `prompt=create` (enrol a new member): pre-fill your registration form with the pushed
  enrolment claims and let the customer register. If the pushed data matches an existing
  membership, offer sign-in and link the account; never create a duplicate.

Show your Terms and Conditions and privacy policy and collect any consent you require.

On completion, redirect back (HTTP 302) to the `redirect_uri` from the stored PAR,
appending `code`, `state`, and `iss` on success, or `error`, `state`, and `iss` on
failure. `iss` is your issuer URL (RFC 9207): Revolut rejects a response whose `iss`
doesn't match the issuer it started the flow with. Bind the membership server-side to
the authorisation code; never put personal data or `member_id` in the redirect URL.

If the `request_uri` is unknown, expired, or already used, there is no stored request and
no `state` to return: redirect to the redirect URI registered for `client_id` with
`error=invalid_request_uri` and `iss`. If no valid redirect URI is known for the
`client_id`, render an error page instead of redirecting.

Reject authorisation requests that bypass `request_uri` (raw OAuth parameters) with `400`,
and render an error page for the customer.

As a browser-facing endpoint, this operation carries no credentials, correlation ID
(`Request-Id`), or API-version header.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Revolut's OAuth 2.0 client ID, as registered during onboarding.

302.description:
Redirect back to Revolut, with `iss` percent-encoded in the query string. Success:
`Location: {redirect_uri}?code={authorization_code}&state={state}&iss={issuer}`.
Failure: `Location: {redirect_uri}?error={error}&state={state}&iss={issuer}` with one
of the following errors:

| Error | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `access_denied` | The customer refused to continue or, in the link flow, has no account with you. Revolut ends the flow. |
| `invalid_request_uri` | Unknown, expired, or already-used `request_uri`. Sent without `state`. Revolut shows an error and the customer can start again from Revolut Wallet. |
| `temporarily_unavailable` | Temporary error; the customer can retry. |

This response has no body.

Location.description: The redirect target, the `redirect_uri` from the stored PAR with the result appended.

success.summary: The customer enrolled or linked their membership

400.description:
The request bypassed `request_uri` or is otherwise invalid, and no redirect back to
Revolut is possible. Render an error page for the customer.

post.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749): the `token_endpoint` in your discovery document.
Revolut's backend calls it server-to-server for the following grants:

- `authorization_code`: exchange the code from the browser redirect, together with the
  Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) `code_verifier` (RFC 7636). Check that the verifier
  matches the `code_challenge` stored with the Pushed Authorization Request (PAR), and
  include an `id_token` (OpenID Connect).
- `client_credentials`: server-to-server access tokens Revolut uses for
  `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` (scope `loyalty.enrol`) and, if you accept OAuth 2.0 there,
  `POST /loyalty/apply` (scope `loyalty.apply`).

**ID token.** A JSON Web Token (JWT) signed with a key published at your `jwks_uri`, using
the algorithm agreed during onboarding (`RS256` or `ES256`). Include the following
claims: `iss` (your issuer URL), `sub` (your stable identifier for the customer), `aud`
(Revolut's `client_id`), `exp`, `iat`, `nonce` (matching the PAR), and `member_id` (the
membership the customer enrolled in or linked). Revolut validates the signature, `iss`,
`aud`, `exp`, and `nonce`, and ends the flow if any check fails.

Authenticate Revolut on every grant (client secret, private key JWT, or mutual TLS
(mTLS), as registered during onboarding) and reject any unauthenticated request with
`401` (`invalid_client`). Unless mTLS is the registered method, Revolut sends a client
secret or JWT assertion in the request body; that's why `security` lists mTLS as
optional.

Authorisation codes are single-use and valid for 5 minutes. Reject a replayed code, or a
`code_verifier` that doesn't match, with `400` (`invalid_grant`). Don't consume the code
when you return `429` or `503`: Revolut retries the exchange with the same code. Return
every token response with `Cache-Control: no-store` (RFC 6749, section 5.1).

parameters.description: Revolut's correlation ID for this request. You may ignore it; echoing it is optional on authorisation-server endpoints.

authorization_code_grant.summary: Exchange the code from the browser redirect

client_credentials_grant.summary: Get a server-to-server token for automatic enrolment

200.description: Tokens issued. Which fields appear depends on the grant.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`, so no cache keeps the tokens (RFC 6749, section 5.1).

400.description:
Malformed or invalid token request (RFC 6749, section 5.2). Authorisation codes are
single-use: a used, expired, mismatched, or replayed code, or a `code_verifier` that
doesn't match the stored `code_challenge`, returns `invalid_grant`.

value.error_description: The request is missing a required parameter or is otherwise malformed.
The authorisation code is invalid, expired, or already used, or the code verifier doesn't match.
The grant type is not supported by this authorisation server.

401.description:
Client authentication failed (`invalid_client`): Revolut's client credentials are
missing, unknown, or invalid for the registered client-authentication method.

get.description:
:::warning [Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Revolut's backend calls this once per enrolment or link, immediately after exchanging the
authorisation code at your token endpoint, to fetch the membership the customer just
enrolled in or linked. Return the membership identifiers, its current loyalty state, and
the complete pass envelope for the customer's Revolut Wallet. The `member_id` you return
must equal the `member_id` claim of the ID token you issued for the same code.

After this call, keep the pass current through
[pass updates](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/operations/update-pass): push changes through
the Wallet Partner API, or serve Revolut's poll requests.

Validate the access token your authorisation server issued and require the
`loyalty.profile` scope. Revolut uses the token only for this endpoint, including any
retries after `429` or `503`, so issue a short-lived access token whose lifetime still
covers the `Retry-After` delays you return. Signal token errors in the `WWW-Authenticate`
header (RFC 6750): reject a request without a token with `401` and a bare `Bearer`
challenge, an expired or invalid token with `401` (`invalid_token`), and a token without
`loyalty.profile` with `403` (`insufficient_scope`).

When the customer unlinks the membership in Revolut Wallet, Revolut doesn't notify you; it
stops calling your loyalty endpoints for that membership.

200.description:
The membership's profile: its identifiers, current loyalty state, and the complete
pass envelope.

profile.summary: Enrolled membership profile, with a pass that uses your template

401.description:
No access token, or an expired or invalid one. For a request without a token, send a
bare `Bearer` challenge with no error code (RFC 6750, section 3.1). For an expired or
invalid token (not issued for this enrolment or link, expired, or failing
validation), send `invalid_token`. Signal the error in `WWW-Authenticate`; the JSON
body is optional.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bearer challenge carrying the OAuth 2.0 error code (RFC 6750).
WWW-Authenticate.example: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The access token expired"

value.error_description: The access token expired or is invalid.

403.description:
The access token lacks the `loyalty.profile` scope (`insufficient_scope`). Signal the
error in `WWW-Authenticate` (RFC 6750); the JSON body is optional.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bearer challenge carrying the OAuth 2.0 error code and the required scope (RFC 6750).

value.error_description: The access token does not have the loyalty.profile scope.

404.description: No active membership found for this access token. Revolut stops retrying.

value.message: No active membership found for this token.

mtls.description:
**Mutual TLS (mTLS).** Revolut presents a client certificate signed by the Revolut
Partner CA. Validate it against the Revolut CA chain from onboarding and reject any
request without a valid Revolut certificate. Your Partner ID is bound to it. Can be
used on its own, or layered on top of JSON Web Signature (JWS) signing for defence
in depth.

A failed mTLS handshake terminates at the TLS layer and produces no HTTP response.
Return `401` only when the connection was established but the client certificate is
missing, untrusted, or not bound to your Partner ID (for example, when TLS
terminates at a proxy in front of your application).

jws.name: Jws-Signature
jws.description:
**Message signing (JSON Web Signature, JWS).** Revolut signs every request as a
detached JWS (RFC 7515, Appendix F) and sends the compact serialisation in the
`Jws-Signature` header.
Verify it exactly as follows:

- **Signed bytes.** The signature covers the exact raw HTTP request body bytes as
  transmitted; nothing is re-serialised or re-encoded. The JWS uses
  `b64: false` (RFC 7797), so to verify, take the body bytes you received, verbatim,
  as the JWS payload.
- **Protected JOSE header.** `alg` (`RS256` or `ES256`), `kid` (the ID of the
  Revolut Partner signing key whose certificate you registered during onboarding),
  `iat` (integer Unix epoch seconds, UTC, when the signature was created),
  `b64: false`, and `crit: ["b64", "iat"]`.
- **Replay protection.** Reject any request where `iat` differs from your current
  time by more than 5 minutes, allowing for clock skew.
- **Key selection and rotation.** Verify only against the registered key whose
  `kid` matches the header. Revolut may register a new key (new `kid`) and keep the
  previous key valid for an overlap window before revoking it; accept any
  registered, unrevoked `kid`.
- **Integrity scope.** The signature covers the request body only. The
  `Idempotency-Key`, `Request-Id`, HTTP method, path, and `Revolut-Api-Version`
  headers are not integrity-protected; TLS (optionally mTLS) and the
  `Idempotency-Key` semantics cover them.

May be used on its own or together with mTLS.

oauth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 **client credentials**. Revolut requests a short-lived access token from your
token endpoint, the `token_endpoint` in your discovery document (authenticating with its
onboarding credential: `client_secret`, `private_key_jwt`, or its mTLS certificate), and
sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token carries the scopes Revolut
requests (`loyalty.apply`, `loyalty.enrol`). May be used on its own or together with
mTLS.

scopes.loyalty.enrol: Enrol customers into your loyalty program server-to-server.

accessToken.description:
Access token issued by your authorisation server at its token endpoint for the
customer's enrolment or link. It must carry the `loyalty.profile` scope and is sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

ApiVersion.name: Revolut-Api-Version
ApiVersion.description:
Contract version Revolut is calling with. Currently `2026-09-17`.

:::note
If you receive a version you do not implement, respond with `400`.
:::

AuthServerApiVersion.name: Revolut-Api-Version
AuthServerApiVersion.description:
Contract version Revolut is calling with. Revolut sends it to your authorisation server
too, but you may ignore it there: never reject a request because of this header.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
UUID scoped to your Partner ID and identifying one logical operation. Revolut
reuses it for every retry.

**Key lifecycle.** Only a `200` completes and consumes the key: store the key with
its request body and response, and replay the stored response when the key is seen
again. Retryable responses (`202` on `POST /loyalty/apply` only, `429`, and `503`)
must not complete or consume the key. Terminal failures (`400`, `401`, `403`, `404`,
`409`, `410`) need not be retained, as Revolut does not retry them, but if you retain
them anyway, replay the stored result for that key. Retain completed keys and their
responses for at least 7 days.

**Body comparison.** The same key with a different request body returns `409`.
"Different" is semantic, not byte-for-byte: two bodies are the same if their parsed
JSON is equal, regardless of key order or insignificant whitespace; any difference
in field values is a conflict.

RequestId.name: Request-Id
RequestId.description: Revolut's correlation ID for this request. Echo it back in your response.
Correlation ID for the response. Echo the incoming `Request-Id` when present.

RetryAfter.description:
Integer seconds Revolut should wait before retrying (not the HTTP-date form). `0` means
retry immediately. If a retryable response omits this header, Revolut uses its default
backoff schedule.

ApplyLoyaltyRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /loyalty/apply`. Contains the partner-issued membership and program
identifiers recorded during enrolment or linking, plus the transaction context to match.

member_id.description:
Partner-issued identifier of the customer's loyalty membership, recorded when the
customer enrolled or linked an existing membership through Revolut Wallet.

program_id.description:
Partner-issued identifier of the loyalty program associated with the membership,
recorded during enrolment or linking.

PointsEarned.description:
Result of applying a loyalty card to a transaction: the `outcome`, the points the
purchase earned, and optionally the customer's new balance. Revolut ignores unknown
fields in this response, so you may add fields without breaking compatibility.

outcome.description:
Why the customer earned what they did:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `applied` | The membership matched and the loyalty card was applied. `points_earned` contains the points awarded under your program rules. |
| `no_points_earned` | The membership matched and the loyalty card was applied, but the purchase earned no points. `points_earned.value` must be zero, written as `"0"` or a decimal equivalent such as `"0.000000"` (see `PointsAmount.value`). |

points_balance.description:
The customer's new points balance after this transaction. Include it if you track
balances; when you do, `value` and `unit` are required, and `unit` must match
`points_earned.unit`.

PointsAmount.description: The points earned for this transaction.

value.description:
Points earned as a non-negative decimal string with up to six fractional digits. Do
not use a sign, exponent notation, or redundant leading zeros. Compare values as
decimals, so `"72.5"` and `"72.500000"` are equivalent. When the purchase earns no
points, use zero: `"0"` or a decimal equivalent such as `"0.000000"`.

unit.description: Unit label for the points (e.g. points, miles).

monetary_value.description: Optional monetary equivalent of the earned points.

Error.description:
Standard error body for 4xx/5xx responses from `POST /loyalty/apply`,
`POST /loyalty/auto-enrol`, and `GET /loyalty/profile`. Access-token errors on
`GET /loyalty/profile` (`401`, `403`) use `OAuthError` instead.

error_id.description: Your trace ID, if you have one.

OAuthError.description:
Standard OAuth 2.0 error body (RFC 6749, section 5.2). Used by `400` and `401` from
`POST /oauth2/par` (RFC 9126 applies the same format) and `POST /oauth2/token`, and by
access-token errors (`401`, `403`) on `GET /loyalty/profile`, where you signal the error
in the `WWW-Authenticate` header (RFC 6750) and the JSON body is optional. Off-the-shelf
authorisation servers emit this format natively.

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `invalid_request` | The request is missing a required parameter, is otherwise malformed, or repeats a parameter. |
| `invalid_client` | Client authentication failed: unknown client, no authentication included, or an unsupported authentication method. |
| `invalid_grant` | The authorisation code is invalid, expired, already used, issued to another client, or does not match the request, or the `code_verifier` does not match the `code_challenge`. |
| `unauthorized_client` | The authenticated client is not authorised to use this grant type. |
| `unsupported_grant_type` | The grant type is not supported by this authorisation server. |
| `invalid_scope` | The requested scope is invalid, unknown, or malformed. |
| `invalid_token` | The access token expired, was revoked, is malformed, or is otherwise invalid (RFC 6750). |
| `insufficient_scope` | The access token lacks the scope the request needs (RFC 6750). |

error.description: Machine-readable OAuth 2.0 error code; see the table above.

error_description.description:
Human-readable text explaining the error (RFC 6749, section 5.2). Never include
sensitive client credentials in it.

error_uri.description: URI of a page with more information about the error (RFC 6749, section 5.2).

EnrolmentClaims.description:
The details the customer agreed to share for enrolment. `given_name`, `family_name`,
`email`, and `phone_number` come from the customer's Revolut profile and are verified by
Revolut's know your customer (KYC) checks. `custom_fields` are entered by the customer
and are not verified. Which claims are required and which are optional is defined per
partner during onboarding; Revolut sends only the claims agreed in your configuration.
Ignore any claim keys you do not recognise. On `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol`, at least one
claim is always sent.

given_name.description: The customer's given name, verified by Revolut.

family_name.description: The customer's family name, verified by Revolut.

email.description: The customer's email address, verified by Revolut.

phone_number.description: The customer's phone number in E.164 format, verified by Revolut.

custom_fields.description:
Partner-configured enrolment fields the customer entered, keyed by the field
identifier agreed during onboarding (for example, vehicle type or licence plate).
Revolut does not verify them.

AutoEnrolRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol`: the enrolment claims the customer agreed
to share, plus the loyalty program to enrol them in when you operate several. At least
one enrolment claim is always present.

program_id.description:
Partner-issued identifier of the loyalty program the customer selected in Revolut
Wallet. Revolut sends it only if you operate several loyalty programs; the valid
values are agreed during onboarding.

AutoEnrolResult.description:
Result of an automatic enrolment: the identifiers of the membership you created, plus the
complete loyalty pass envelope for the customer's Revolut Wallet. Revolut ignores
unknown fields in this response, so you may add fields without breaking compatibility.

member_id.description:
Partner-issued identifier of the new membership. Revolut records it at enrolment
and sends it back on `POST /loyalty/apply`.

program_id.description:
Partner-issued identifier of the loyalty program. Always returned, even when you
operate a single program, so Revolut can record it for `POST /loyalty/apply`.

points_balance.description: The customer's current points balance. Include it if you track balances.

pass.description:
The complete loyalty pass envelope for the new membership, in any format accepted
by `POST /passes` on the [Wallet Partner API](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/api/revolut-wallet-partner). Its
`partner_reference` is your stable key for the pass. To apply one of your
[templates](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/operations/template-management), set
`template_id` in the envelope; without it, the pass uses only the styling it carries.

AuthServerMetadata.description:
Your authorisation server metadata (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0, with the fields that
RFC 8414, RFC 9126, and RFC 9207 add). The arrays must include the values described
below; extra values and extra fields are allowed.

issuer.description:
Your issuer URL, as registered during onboarding. It must match the `iss` claim of
your ID tokens and the `iss` parameter on your authorisation responses.

authorization_endpoint.description: URL of your authorisation endpoint (`GET /oauth2/authorize` in this reference).

token_endpoint.description: URL of your token endpoint (`POST /oauth2/token` in this reference).

pushed_authorization_request_endpoint.description: URL of your PAR endpoint (`POST /oauth2/par` in this reference, RFC 9126).

jwks_uri.description:
URL of your JSON Web Key Set (JWKS, RFC 7517): the public keys that sign your ID
tokens.

subject_types_supported.description: Subject identifier types you support, for example `public`.

id_token_signing_alg_values_supported.description:
Must include `RS256`, as OpenID Connect Discovery requires. `ES256` is also accepted;
the algorithm you sign with is agreed during onboarding.

require_pushed_authorization_requests.description: Must be `true`. Your authorisation endpoint accepts only requests pushed through PAR.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description: Must be `true`. Every authorisation response carries `iss` (RFC 9207).

prompt_values_supported.description: Must include `login` and `create` (OpenID Connect Prompt Create).

grant_types_supported.description:
Must include `authorization_code`, and `client_credentials` if you implement
`POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` or accept OAuth 2.0 on `POST /loyalty/apply`.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description:
Must include the client-authentication method registered for Revolut:
`client_secret_post`, `private_key_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, or
`self_signed_tls_client_auth`. Revolut never uses `client_secret_basic`.

token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_s.description:
Algorithms you accept for private key JWT client assertions. Required when
`token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` includes `private_key_jwt` (RFC 8414).

mtls_endpoint_aliases.description:
Endpoint URLs that require mTLS (RFC 8705), when mTLS is your registered
client-authentication method. Revolut uses them instead of the standard endpoint
URLs.

scopes_supported.description:
Scopes you support, for example `openid`, `loyalty.profile`, `loyalty.enrol`, and
`loyalty.apply`.

ParRequest.description:
Form body for `POST /oauth2/par` (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), per the Pushed
Authorization Request (PAR) flow (RFC 9126). Carries the OAuth 2.0 authorisation request
parameters, Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE, RFC 7636), and the enrolment claims:
enrolment requests carry the customer's claims, and link requests carry none (see
`enrolment_claims`).

client_id.description: Revolut's OAuth 2.0 client ID, as registered during onboarding.

client_secret.description:
Revolut's client secret. Omit it when the registered client-authentication method
is private key JWT or mTLS.

client_assertion_type.description:
Client-assertion type, used when the registered client-authentication method is
private key JWT (RFC 7521).

client_assertion.description:
The signed JWT assertion authenticating Revolut's client, used with
`client_assertion_type` for private key JWT authentication.

redirect_uri.description: The registered Revolut redirect URI the customer's browser returns to.

response_type.description: OAuth 2.0 response type. This flow always uses the authorisation-code grant.

scope.description:
The scopes Revolut requests: always `openid loyalty.profile`. `openid` makes your
token endpoint issue an ID token (OpenID Connect).

state.description:
Opaque value Revolut sends and expects back, unchanged, on the redirect. Single-use
and short-lived.

nonce.description:
OpenID Connect nonce. Echo it in the `nonce` claim of the ID token issued at
your token endpoint.

prompt.description:
How to route the customer at your authorisation endpoint:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `login` | Forced re-authentication: route the customer straight to your sign-in screen, ignoring any existing session. Revolut sends it when the customer links an existing account, and after `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` returns `account_exists`. |
| `create` | Route the customer straight to your registration screen. Revolut sends it after `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` returns a `403` UI-required code other than `account_exists`, or directly when you don't implement auto-enrol. |

code_challenge.description:
PKCE code challenge: the base64url-encoded SHA-256 hash of the `code_verifier` Revolut
later sends to your token endpoint (RFC 7636). Store it with the request.

program_id.description:
Partner-issued identifier of the loyalty program the customer selected in Revolut
Wallet: the program to enrol them in, or the program whose membership they want to
link. Revolut sends it only if you operate several loyalty programs; the valid values
are agreed during onboarding.

enrolment_claims.description:
JSON-serialised enrolment claims: a flat `EnrolmentClaims` object with the details
the customer agreed to share. An empty JSON object (`{}`) means no personal data is
shared: Revolut sends it in the link flow (`prompt=login`), where the customer
identifies themselves by signing in to you.

ParResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /oauth2/par`: the single-use `request_uri` and how long it
stays valid.

request_uri.description:
Single-use reference to the stored authorisation request. Consumable exactly once
at your authorisation endpoint.

TokenRequest.description:
Form body for `POST /oauth2/token` (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), per the
OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749). Which fields apply depends on the grant and on the
client-authentication method registered during onboarding.

grant_type.description:
The OAuth 2.0 grant being exercised:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `authorization_code` | Exchange the single-use code from the browser redirect, with the PKCE `code_verifier`. |
| `client_credentials` | Obtain a server-to-server token for `POST /loyalty/auto-enrol` (scope `loyalty.enrol`) or `POST /loyalty/apply` (scope `loyalty.apply`). |

code.description:
The authorisation code from the browser redirect. Single-use and valid for 5 minutes;
required with the `authorization_code` grant.

redirect_uri.description: Must match the `redirect_uri` from the PAR. Required with the `authorization_code` grant.

code_verifier.description:
PKCE code verifier (RFC 7636): the secret whose SHA-256 hash Revolut sent as
`code_challenge` on the PAR. Required with the `authorization_code` grant; reject a
mismatch with `invalid_grant`.

scope.description:
The scopes Revolut requests with the `client_credentials` grant: `loyalty.enrol`,
`loyalty.apply`, or both. Not sent with the `authorization_code` grant.

client_id.description:
Revolut's OAuth 2.0 client ID, as registered during onboarding. Revolut always
sends `client_id` in the request body, including when the registered
client-authentication method is mTLS.

client_secret.description:
Revolut's client secret. Omit it when the registered client-authentication method
is private key JWT or mTLS.

client_assertion_type.description:
Client-assertion type, used when the registered client-authentication method is
private key JWT (RFC 7521).

client_assertion.description:
The signed JWT assertion authenticating Revolut's client, used with
`client_assertion_type` for private key JWT authentication.

TokenResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /oauth2/token` (RFC 6749). `id_token` appears only with the
`authorization_code` grant.

access_token.description: The access token Revolut presents to your loyalty API.

expires_in.description:
Seconds before the access token expires. Keep tokens from the `authorization_code`
grant short-lived: Revolut uses them only once, for `GET /loyalty/profile`.

id_token.description:
OpenID Connect ID token (JWT compact serialisation), issued with the
`authorization_code` grant. Sign it with a key published at your `jwks_uri` and
include the `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, `nonce`, and `member_id` claims (see
`POST /oauth2/token`).

scope.description: The scopes the access token carries.

LoyaltyProfile.description:
Response body for `GET /loyalty/profile`: the identifiers of the membership the customer
enrolled in or linked, its current loyalty state, and the complete pass envelope.
Revolut ignores unknown fields in this response, so you may add fields without breaking
compatibility.

member_id.description: Partner-issued identifier of the enrolled or linked membership.

program_id.description: Partner-issued identifier of the loyalty program.

points_balance.description: Current points balance. Include it if you track balances.

pass.description:
The complete loyalty pass envelope, in any format accepted by `POST /passes` on the
[Wallet Partner API](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/api/revolut-wallet-partner). Its `partner_reference` is
your stable key for the pass when you push updates later. To apply one of your
[templates](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/operations/template-management), set
`template_id` in the envelope; without it, the pass uses only the styling it carries.

Money.description: ISO 4217 monetary amount, represented as strings to preserve decimal precision. Amounts are non-negative.

amount.description: Non-negative decimal amount as a string (e.g. "72.40").

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. GBP, EUR, USD).

LoyaltyTransactionContext.description:
Identifiers Revolut supplies so you can match the originating transaction.

**Authoritative matching algorithm.** Use `rrn` + `merchant_id` to find candidate
transactions. Confirm a candidate only when `transaction_at` is within ±24 hours of the
timestamp you hold, `total.currency` is the same, and the decimal numeric value of
`total.amount` is exactly equal. Compare amounts as decimal numbers rather than raw strings, so
`"72.4"` and `"72.40"` are equal. If no transaction matches, return `404` with
`transaction_not_found`. If more than one transaction matches all fields, return `409` with
`ambiguous_transaction`; Revolut stops retrying and flags the case for investigation.

Revolut uses the acquiring institution ID collected during onboarding to route eligible
transactions. This routing identifier is not included in `transaction_context`.

rrn.description: ISO 8583 Retrieval Reference Number of the original payment.

merchant_id.description: Card acceptor identifier (DE 42 in ISO 8583 messaging); identifies the sub-merchant for aggregators.

transaction_at.description:
Timestamp of the purchase in UTC and ISO 8601 format. Accept it as a match only when it is
within ±24 hours of the timestamp you hold for the transaction.

total.description:
Transaction total used to confirm the match. Require the same currency and exact decimal
numeric amount; do not apply a tolerance for authorised-versus-settled differences.

PointsBalance.description: Points balance for a loyalty pass.

value.description:
Current points balance as a non-negative decimal string with up to six fractional digits.
Do not use a sign, exponent notation, or redundant leading zeros. Compare values as decimals,
so `"1500"` and `"1500.00"` are equivalent.

unit.description: Unit label for the balance (e.g. points, miles).

monetary_value.description: Optional monetary equivalent of the points balance.

PartnerPassRevision.description: Fields that identify a partner's pass and the revision being submitted.

partner_reference.description:
Your own reference for the pass; use it to match the pass in your system. Immutable after
creation. On `PUT /passes/{id}`, it must match the pass addressed in the path; a mismatch
is rejected with `422`.

version.description:
Your pass revision. Must be `1` on create. On update, must equal the currently stored
version exactly plus one: reusing an already-stored version, replaying an older one, or
skipping ahead are all rejected with `409` (`stale_version`).

RevPassFormat.description: Format discriminator for a Revolut native pass.

TemplateId.description: Revolut-assigned UUID that identifies a pass template.

RevPassCreateTemplate.description: Optional Revolut template selection for a native pass at creation.

template_id.description:
UUID of an active template created through the template management endpoints of the
Partner API. If omitted, no template is applied: the pass uses only the styling it
carries. Set at creation and immutable; not accepted when updating a pass. A
`template_id` that doesn't exist under your Partner ID returns `404`
(`template_not_found`); a `draft` or `terminated` template returns `422`
(`template_not_active`).

SharingOptions.description:
Sharing options controlling which customers can install and hold a pass. A pass-level value
takes precedence over the template's value; when neither sets one, `ONE_USER_ALL_DEVICES`
applies.

When a customer adds the pass, Revolut checks the holder mode resolved this way: with
`MULTIPLE_HOLDERS`, anyone who receives the pass can install it and the first customer to add
it becomes its owner; with `ONE_USER_ALL_DEVICES`, only the pass's owner can hold it, across
all of their devices.

holder_mode.description:
Who can install and hold the pass:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `MULTIPLE_HOLDERS` | Any customer who receives the pass can install and hold it. The first customer to add the pass becomes its owner. |
| `ONE_USER_ALL_DEVICES` | A single customer holds the pass, across all of their devices. |

PassSharingOptions.description: Optional sharing options for a pass at creation.

sharing_options.description:
Who can install and hold this pass. Set at creation and immutable; not accepted when
updating a pass. Takes precedence over the template's sharing options: when omitted on a
pass created with a `template_id`, Revolut uses the template's holder mode at install time,
and when there is no template either, the default `ONE_USER_ALL_DEVICES` applies.

Image.description: An image used by pass branding.

asset_ref.description: Reference to an image asset managed by Revolut.

ColourScheme.description: Explicit colours used to render a branded pass.

Branding.description: Optional visual branding for a pass.

brand_name.description: Brand name displayed on the pass.

logo.description: Logo image used by the pass.

background_image.description: Background or hero image used by the pass.

predefined_style.description: Predefined visual style for the pass.

colours.description: Explicit colour scheme for the pass.

Issuer.description: Issuer information displayed on a pass.

issuer_id.description:
Revolut-managed identifier of the issuer. Revolut derives this value from the authenticated
partner and returns the partner's Revolut-assigned UUID; do not send it in request bodies.

issuer_full_name.description: Full legal name of the issuer.

Barcode.description: A machine-readable barcode displayed on a Revolut native pass.

format.description: Symbology used to render the barcode.

type.description: Payload type. Only static barcode payloads are supported.

static_payload.description: Static value encoded in the barcode.

default.description: Fallback text when no localisation matches.

localisation_key.description:
Key resolved at render time against the template's localisation map, then Revolut's
localisation catalogue (Revolut-curated translations for standard pass strings), falling
back to the `default` text.

Action.description: A button rendered on the pass (e.g. "Open website", "Get directions").

id.description: Unique identifier for the action within this pass.

type.description: Documented values: `open_external_url`. External URL domain needs to be registered at onboarding.

label.description: Display label for the button, with optional localisation.

importance.description: Relative prominence of this action (5 = primary, 1 = least prominent).

Presentation.description: How a trigger is presented to the customer.

title.description: Title text for the notification or tile, with optional localisation.

description.description: Body text for the notification or tile, with optional localisation.

Trigger.description: A context-aware notification that nudges the customer (e.g. proximity alert, time before event).

id.description: Unique identifier for the trigger within this pass.

importance.description: Relative prominence of this trigger (5 = high, 1 = low).

time_offset.description: ISO 8601 duration before the target (e.g. `PT1H` for 1 hour before departure).

radius_meters.description: Radius in meters around the `location_targets` coordinates for the proximity alert.

field_target.description: Name of the semantic field to watch for changes (e.g. `boarding.gate`).

presentation.description: How the trigger is presented to the customer (notification, tile).

RevPassBaseContent.description: Fields common to every Revolut native pass content type.

relevant_at.description:
When the pass becomes time-relevant (departure, event start); drives Revolut's polling
cadence. Derived from semantic content if omitted.

branding.description: Optional visual branding for the pass.

issuer.description: Optional issuer information displayed on the pass.

barcodes.description:
Barcodes displayed on the pass. If the pass uses a template, omit this field to inherit the
template barcodes, send a non-empty array to replace the complete template array, or send an
empty array to suppress all template barcodes. If the pass doesn't use a template, omitting
this field means that the pass has no barcodes.

triggers.description: Context-aware notifications that nudge the customer.

Passenger.description: Passenger details for a boarding pass.

full_name.description: Full name of the passenger as it appears on the boarding pass.

fare_class.description: Human-readable fare class (e.g. Economy, Business, First).

fare_class_code.description: IATA fare class code (single letter, e.g. Y for Economy, J for Business).

frequent_flyer_program.description: Name of the frequent flyer program the passenger belongs to.

frequent_flyer_number.description: Membership number within the frequent flyer program.

name.description: Full name of the airport (e.g. London Luton Airport).

city.description: City where the airport is located.

Flight.description: Flight details for a boarding pass.

flight_number.description: Flight number without the carrier code (e.g. 2241, not SJ2241).

carrier_name.description: Display name of the operating carrier.

operating_carrier_code.description: IATA (2-character) or ICAO (3-character) carrier code of the actual operating carrier (for codeshare flights, this may differ from `carrier_code`).

aircraft_type.description: IATA aircraft type code (e.g. A320, B738).

Boarding.description: Boarding details for a flight (gate, seat, and boarding time).

gate.description: Boarding gate at the departure airport.

boarding_group.description: Boarding group or zone (airline-specific, e.g. A, B, 1, 2).

sequence_number.description: Boarding sequence number assigned to the passenger.

seat_class.description: Seat class label (e.g. Economy, Premium Economy, Business).

Booking.description: Booking details for a boarding pass.

pnr.description: Passenger Name Record, the booking reference from the airline's reservation system.

booking_reference.description: Alternative booking reference (e.g. agency or GDS reference), if different from the PNR.

Validity.description: Validity window for a pass (when it becomes active and when it expires).

valid_from.description: Start of the pass validity period, UTC, ISO 8601.

valid_until.description: End of the pass validity period, UTC, ISO 8601.

BoardingPassSemantics.description: Semantic tags for a boarding pass.

validity.description: Optional validity window for the pass.

RevPassBoardingContent.description: The native content of a boarding pass.

RevPassCreateBoardingContent.description: The native content of a boarding pass at creation.

Event.description: Event details for an event pass.

edition.description: Edition or iteration of a recurring event (e.g. 2026, Season 5).

held_on.description: Calendar day of the event (use `starts_at` for the precise start time).

starts_at.description: Start time of the event, UTC, ISO 8601.

ends_at.description: End time of the event, UTC, ISO 8601.

doors_open_at.description: Time the venue doors open, UTC, ISO 8601.

city.description: City where the venue is located.

section.description: Section or block within the venue (e.g. Block 112, Section C).

Ticket.description: Ticket details for an event pass.

booking_reference.description: Booking or order reference for the ticket purchase.

Participant.description: Participant details for an event pass (e.g. conference attendee).

company.description: Company or organisation the participant represents.

role.description: Role or title at the event (e.g. Speaker, Attendee, Volunteer).

name.description: Name of the organising company or individual.

EventPassSemantics.description: Semantic tags for an event pass.

validity.description: Optional validity window for the pass.

RevPassEventContent.description: The native content of an event pass.

RevPassCreateEventContent.description: The native content of an event pass at creation.

Member.description: Member details for a loyalty pass.

full_name.description: Full name of the loyalty program member.

member_id.description: Membership number or ID within the loyalty program.

member_since_on.description: Date the member joined the programme.

TierProgress.description: Progress towards the next loyalty tier.

current.description: Current progress value as a string (e.g. points earned this period).

target.description: Target value required to reach the next tier, as a string.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the progress values (e.g. points, stays, flights).

NextReward.description: Next reward the member can unlock with their points.

description.description: Human-readable description of the reward (e.g. "Free coffee voucher").

points_required.description: Points required to unlock the reward, as a string.

Loyalty.description: Loyalty program details for a pass.

program_name.description: Display name of the loyalty program.

tier.description: Current tier level of the member (e.g. Gold, Silver, Bronze).

next_reward.description: Next reward the member can unlock.

LoyaltyPassSemantics.description: Semantic tags for a loyalty pass.

loyalty.description: Loyalty program details (tier, balance, next reward).

validity.description: Optional validity window for the pass.

FieldId.description: Unique identifier for a custom field within a generic pass.

DataCategory.description:
Data category for the field. The category describes the type of information carried by
the field.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `identity` | Primary subjects, holder names, pass titles, or card names. |
| `status` | State metrics, membership tiers, or operational updates such as Delayed, Gold Tier, or Active. |
| `time` | Temporal coordinates such as Start Time 19:00, boarding times, or expiry times. |
| `location` | Spatial coordinates or places such as Seat 14C, Gate A7, venues, or addresses. |
| `verification` | Human-readable fallback codes, member IDs, or order references. |
| `attribute` | Domain properties such as Meal: Vegan, Class: Business, or Points: 1,400. |
| `governance` | Contractual, legal, or reference information such as terms, disclaimers, or support phone numbers. |

FieldSemanticType.description:
Optional semantic tag associated with the field. 

The following values are currently exposed by the typed pass schemas in current API version.
Use the public snake_case path names.

**Boarding passes**

`passenger.full_name`, `passenger.fare_class`, `passenger.fare_class_code`,
`passenger.frequent_flyer_program`, `passenger.frequent_flyer_number`, `flight.flight_number`,
`flight.carrier_code`, `flight.carrier_name`, `flight.operating_carrier_code`,
`flight.departure_airport.iata`, `flight.departure_airport.name`, `flight.departure_airport.city`,
`flight.departure_airport.country_code`, `flight.departure_airport.terminal`,
`flight.arrival_airport.iata`, `flight.arrival_airport.name`, `flight.arrival_airport.city`,
`flight.arrival_airport.country_code`, `flight.arrival_airport.terminal`,
`flight.scheduled_departure_at`, `flight.scheduled_arrival_at`, `flight.aircraft_type`,
`boarding.gate`, `boarding.boarding_at`, `boarding.boarding_group`, `boarding.sequence_number`,
`boarding.seat`, `boarding.seat_class`, `booking.pnr`, `booking.ticket_number`,
`booking.booking_reference`, `validity.valid_from`, `validity.valid_until`.

**Event passes**

`event.name`, `event.category`, `event.edition`, `event.held_on`, `event.starts_at`,
`event.ends_at`, `event.doors_open_at`, `venue.name`, `venue.address`, `venue.city`,
`venue.country_code`, `venue.coordinates.lat`, `venue.coordinates.lng`, `venue.gate`,
`venue.section`, `venue.row`, `venue.seat`, `ticket.number`, `ticket.booking_reference`,
`ticket.type`, `participant.full_name`, `participant.company`, `participant.role`,
`organiser.name`, `validity.valid_from`, `validity.valid_until`.

**Loyalty passes**

`member.full_name`, `member.member_id`, `member.member_since_on`, `loyalty.program_name`,
`loyalty.tier`, `loyalty.tier_progress.current`, `loyalty.tier_progress.target`,
`loyalty.tier_progress.unit`, `loyalty.points_balance.value`, `loyalty.points_balance.unit`,
`loyalty.points_balance.monetary_value.amount`, `loyalty.points_balance.monetary_value.currency`,
`loyalty.next_reward.description`, `loyalty.next_reward.points_required`,
`validity.valid_from`, `validity.valid_until`.

FieldData.description:
Shared content, semantic metadata, and optional formatting hints for a generic-pass custom field.
The field `id` is referenced from the pass `presentation` configuration. When neither the pass
nor its template provides a presentation, every field must provide `data_category` and
`semantic_type`; `importance` remains optional.

label.description: Display label for the field, with optional localisation.

value.description: Display value for the field, with optional localisation.

data_type.description:
Interpretation of the field value. The `value` is always carried as a string (or a
localised string map); `data_type` defines how Revolut parses and renders it:

| Value | Wire representation |
|-------|---------------------|
| `text` | Any string. |
| `number` | Plain decimal number as a string, e.g. `1400` or `1400.50` (no thousands separators; rendered per `number_style`). |
| `currency` | Plain decimal amount as a string, e.g. `1400.50`, with `currency_code` (ISO 4217) alongside. |
| `date_time` | RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, e.g. `2026-09-15T19:00:00.000Z`. |
| `uri` | Absolute HTTPS URI string, e.g. `https://example.com/offer`. |

Conditional rules: `currency` requires `currency_code`; `number_style` applies only to
`number`; `date_style`, `time_style`, `is_relative`, and `ignores_time_zone` apply only
to `date_time`.

data_category.description:
Category describing the information carried by the field. Required on every field when
rendering falls back to semantic metadata; otherwise optional.

semantic_type.description:
Semantic identifier associated with the field. Required on every field when rendering falls
back to semantic metadata; otherwise optional.

importance.description:
Optional relative prominence of the field (5 = highest, 1 = lowest), used for semantic
rendering.

text_alignment.description: Preferred text alignment when the renderer supports it.

date_style.description: Preferred date display style for a `date_time` value.

time_style.description: Preferred time display style for a `date_time` value.

is_relative.description: Whether a date and time value should be presented relative to the current time.

ignores_time_zone.description: Whether a date and time value should be shown without time-zone conversion.

number_style.description: Preferred display style for a numeric value.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code for a `currency` value. Required when `data_type` is `currency`.

RowItem.description: A field placed in a positional presentation row.

field_id.description: ID of the primary field displayed in this slot.

join_field_id.description: Optional ID of a field joined to the primary field in the same slot.

alignment.description: Horizontal placement of the slot within its row.

PresentationRow.description: A row in a positional generic-pass presentation.

PositionalPresentation.description:
Maps field IDs into header, primary, secondary, and footer sections. This layout may be supplied on the
pass or by its template. Every referenced ID must match a field in the pass, and every field ID
must appear at least once as a `field_id` or `join_field_id` when this layout is used.

header.description: Optional header section row, displayed before the primary section.

primary.description: Primary section row, displayed after the header when provided.

secondary.description: Optional secondary section rows, in display order.

PresentationConfig.description:
Optional explicit positional layout for a generic pass. When omitted, the template presentation
is used. When neither provides a presentation, the pass is rendered from semantic metadata on
every field.

RevPassGenericContent.description:
A fields-driven generic pass. The `fields` array defines reusable field data and an optional
`presentation` selects a positional layout. When `presentation` is omitted, the template
presentation is used. When neither provides a presentation, the pass is rendered from semantic
metadata: every field must provide `data_category` and `semantic_type`; `importance` is optional.

fields.description: Custom fields available to the selected presentation layout.

presentation.description:
Optional explicit layout. When omitted, the template presentation is used. When neither
provides a presentation, rendering falls back to semantic metadata on every field.

RevPassCreateGenericContent.description: The native content of a generic pass at creation.

RevPassCreateContent.description:
The content of a Revolut native pass at creation. The root-level `type` discriminator selects
the content structure: `semantics` for typed passes, `fields` with an optional `presentation`
for generic passes. The immutable `template_id`, when used, is set on the containing pass envelope.

RevPassCreateEnvelope.description:
A pass using Revolut's native semantic model, at creation. The root-level `template_id` selects
the render template, while the `rev_pass` object carries the pass type, semantic content, and
relevant-at timestamp.

PkPassBase64Format.description: Format-specific fields for a `.pkpass` file supplied as a base64-encoded string.

pkpass.description:
The raw `.pkpass` file (a signed ZIP archive), base64-encoded as a string. Must decode to
at most 10 MB.

TemplateOverride.description: Optional template override for an imported pass at creation.

template_id.description:
UUID of an active template created through the template management endpoints of the
Partner API. It overrides the source pass's visual design. If omitted, Revolut uses the
branding from the imported source. Set at creation and immutable. A `template_id` that
doesn't exist under your Partner ID returns `404` (`template_not_found`); a `draft` or
`terminated` template returns `422` (`template_not_active`).

PkPassBase64.description:
A pass created from a `.pkpass` file, provided as a base64-encoded string.
Revolut parses the `pass.json` inside, extracts the semantic content, and renders the pass
natively. Images and translations inside the `.pkpass` are used where possible.

PkPassUrlFormat.description: Format-specific fields for a `.pkpass` file supplied through a download URL.

pkpass_url.description:
Public HTTPS URL from which Revolut downloads the `.pkpass` file. Must return a valid
`.pkpass` (signed ZIP archive).

Revolut fetches the URL server-side under these rules:

- HTTPS only; the host must resolve to a publicly reachable address (private, loopback,
  and link-local IP ranges are not fetched).
- At most 3 redirects, each to an HTTPS URL.
- The response must be `200` with a valid `pkpass` body of at most 10 MB, fully received
  within 10 seconds.
- The URL must remain valid for at least 24 hours after submission so Revolut can download
  and re-download it, including across retries.

If the download fails any of these rules, the request is rejected with `422`
(`pkpass_url_download_failed`).

PkPassUrl.description:
A pass created from a `.pkpass` file, provided via a download URL. Revolut fetches
the `.pkpass` file from the URL, parses the `pass.json` inside, extracts the semantic content, and
renders the pass natively. The URL must be publicly accessible and return a valid `.pkpass` file.

WalletObjectsJsonFormat.description: Format-specific fields for a Wallet Objects JSON pass.

type.description:
The Wallet Objects resource family used to validate and render both resources.

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `event_ticket` | An `EventTicketClass` and `EventTicketObject` pair. |
| `flight` | A `FlightClass` and `FlightObject` pair. |
| `generic` | A `GenericClass` and `GenericObject` pair. |
| `gift_card` | A `GiftCardClass` and `GiftCardObject` pair. |
| `loyalty` | A `LoyaltyClass` and `LoyaltyObject` pair. |
| `offer` | An `OfferClass` and `OfferObject` pair. |
| `transit` | A `TransitClass` and `TransitObject` pair. |

id.description: Identifier of the supplied Wallet Objects class resource.

class.description:
The Wallet Objects class resource for the selected `type`. Its `id` must match the
supplied object's `classId`; a mismatch is rejected with `422`
(`walletobjects_class_mismatch`).

id.description: Identifier of the supplied Wallet Objects object resource.

classId.description: Identifier of the supplied class resource; must match `class.id`.

object.description: The Wallet Objects object resource for the selected `type`.

walletobjects.description:
The Wallet Objects resource family and its class/object pair. Send the format-specific fields
as defined by the Wallet Objects contract. Revolut validates both resources against `type`,
parses them, and renders the pass natively.

WalletObjectsPass.description:
A pass in Wallet Objects JSON format, containing an explicit resource family and the corresponding
class/object pair. Revolut parses both resources and renders the pass natively. The object's
`classId` must reference the supplied class resource.

PassCreateEnvelope.description:
A pass being created or provisioned, in any supported format. The `format` field selects the
encoding; see the individual schemas for each variant. The optional `template_id` and
`sharing_options` are always root-level creation settings, regardless of format.

- `revpass`: Revolut's native semantic model. The `rev_pass.type` discriminator further selects the
  content structure: typed passes (`boarding_pass`, `event_pass`, `loyalty_pass`) carry `semantics`;
  generic passes (`generic_pass`) carry `fields` and an optional `presentation` layout.
- `pkpass_base64`: A `.pkpass` file, base64-encoded as a string.
- `pkpass_url`: A URL pointing to a `.pkpass` file for Revolut to download.
- `walletobjects_json`: A Wallet Objects resource family and its class/object pair under `walletobjects`.

This multi-format envelope is available from API version `2026-07-01`. The set of formats is
closed within this API version; new pass formats are published under a new dated API version,
not added to `2026-07-01`. New `rev_pass.type` values may be added over time and are available
in all supported API versions. Requests with an unrecognised `format` value are rejected with `422`
(`unsupported_format`).

Unauthorized.description:
Missing or invalid Revolut credentials: an mTLS certificate rejected at the
application layer (a failed TLS handshake never produces an HTTP response), an
invalid JWS signature, or a missing/invalid OAuth 2.0 access token.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated, but the credential lacks the required scope/permission (e.g. an OAuth
token without the required scope).

value.message: The credential does not have the required scope.

Conflict.description:
Unrecoverable conflict: the `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different request
body, or the transaction match is ambiguous. Revolut stops retrying.

value.message: The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.
Multiple transactions match this rrn, merchant_id, transaction_at, and total.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.

value.message: Rate limit exceeded. Retry after the specified delay.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Temporary capacity issue. Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.

AuthServerRetryLater.description:
Rate limit exceeded (`429`) or temporary capacity issue (`503`) on your authorisation
server. Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`. The body format is not specified.
